shortDefinition: Precision measures how many retrieved items were relevant; recall measures how many relevant items were retrieved.
fullDefinition: Precision and recall are the two core metrics for any system that retrieves or classifies items. Precision answers "of everything I returned, what fraction was actually correct?" Recall answers "of everything that should have been returned, what fraction did I find?" The two trade off against each other: returning more items usually raises recall and lowers precision, and being more selective does the opposite. The F1 score is their harmonic mean, a single number that penalises extreme imbalance. In LLM evaluation they matter most for retrieval-augmented generation and search: a RAG system with low recall never sees the document it needs, while low precision floods the context window with irrelevant text that can derail the answer.
examples: A search returns 10 results, 6 relevant → precision = 0.6
There were 12 relevant documents in total, 6 found → recall = 0.5
